en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
from Abu Abullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If a man was to rent a house for ten Dirhams and he dwells in two-thirds of it and rents out a third of it for ten Dirhams, there would not be a problem with it, and he should not rent it out for more than what he has rented it for unless if he would to innovate something in it (Make some improvement to it)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man rents a house for ten dirham and lives in it, but uses only two-thirds and rents the other one-third for ten dirhams, it is not unlawful but he must not rent out for more than what has rented (which is ten dirham) unless he introduces something in it.’”
